claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous, compositionally uniform, single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Controlled high-strain deformation combined with moderate annealing can induce local compositional fluctuations without causing bulk grain-boundary intermetallic precipitation.
Deformation-induced local compositional segregation is the primary cause of emerging brittleness in an initially single-phase HEA.
Local compositional segregation produces intragranular nanoscale phase separation.
The segregated nanoscale regions have different stacking-fault energies.
Compositionally distinct regions activate mechanically incompatible deformation mechanisms.
The nanoscale phase-separated regions act as internal crack-initiation sites.
High strain and elevated temperature enhance atomic mobility and local elemental redistribution.
Diffusion along dislocation lines and stacking faults promotes local phase separation under load and heat.
One segregated region accommodates deformation by twinning while another accommodates it by dislocation glide.
Differences in local mechanical response create internal stress concentrations and reduce plastic compatibility.
Internal stress concentrations promote premature microcrack nucleation and thereby reduce toughness.
Thermomechanically treated samples will have lower toughness and ductility than the initial homogeneous state.
High-resolution microscopy and compositional mapping will reveal nanoscale compositional segregation after treatment.
Samples containing the induced segregation will have lower fracture toughness than samples in which segregation is suppressed.
The hypothesized embrittling changes occur within grains rather than primarily at grain boundaries.
The mechanism is significant under severe plastic deformation and moderate annealing, below conditions causing extensive grain-boundary precipitation or grain coarsening.
Under very low strain or room-temperature conditions, the alloy largely retains its original toughness.
Single-phase compositionally complex alloys can exhibit high room-temperature toughness and ductility through multiple dislocation and twinning mechanisms.
Some HEA systems exhibit nanoscale phase separation associated with compositional segregation and deformation-induced twinning.
